sheet.name: Name

dodge.name: Dodge
dodge.description: Dodge is your skill at getting out of the way of bullets, energy beams, knives and punches. It is used extensively in personal combat and determines your Defence (Dodge) bonus.

energyWeapons.name: Energy Weapons
energyWeapons.description: Energy Weapons cover all laser and beam weapons used in personal combat, except for those which are shoulder or tripod mounted. The higher your energy weapons Skill the more likely you are to hit and the more damage burst weapons, such as the Assault Beamer, will inflict.

fighting.name: Fighting
fighting.description: Fighting is the skill that governs weaponless combat, such as boxing, wrestling, kung fu, headbutting and any other noble martial art. Fighting can include improvised weapons such as chair legs and broken bottles, but any close combat weapon designed for combat falls under the Melee Weapons Skill. Fighting can be a useful skill for taking opponents alive as the damage it inflicts is (generally) non-lethal.

grenade.name: Grenade
grenade.description: This Skill allows you to use grenades with a semblance of accuracy and safety. It also covers the ability to use and disarm explosives of all kinds.

heavyWeapons.name: Heavy Weapons
heavyWeapons.description: Heavy Weapons are large tripod or shoulder mounted weapons used in Personal Combat such as chain guns, missile launchers and plasma cannons. Heavy Weapons are powerful, but difficult to use and aim in small scale, fast moving skirmishes. This Skill can also be used to fire weapons mounted on vehicles provided that you are personally operating the weapon. If you are relying on the vehicle’s targeting computer you must use the Vehicle Weapons Skill.

kineticWeapons.name: Kinetic Weapons
kineticWeapons.description: Kinetic Weapons cover all projectile based weapons used in personal combat such as autopistols, assault rifles and shotguns. Weapons which are shoulder or tripod mounted use the Heavy Weapons Skill instead. The higher your Kinetic Weapons Skill the more likely you are to hit and the more damage burst weapons will inflict.

meleeWeapons.name: Melee Weapons
meleeWeapons.description: The Melee Weapons Skill covers the use of all close combat weapons such as swords, clubs, and axes as well as more exotic close range weapons such as Cyberclaws. Melee Weapons are rarely used by common folk but are beloved of assassins and expert mercenaries who like to kill cleanly and silently.

parry.name: Parry
parry.description: The Parry Skill is used to deflect close combat attacks, both from Melee Weapons and from fighting. It is very useful as it allows a chance to counter-attack against opponent that misses you. See the chapter on Personal Combat for details.

computer.name: Computer
computer.description: Computers are easy to use in the 34th century, but quite hard to crack. The Computer Skill allows you to hack terminals, interrogate secured databases and even to reprogram the computer’s basic functions.

cultureLaw.name: Culture & Law
cultureLaw.description: Culture and Law is your knowledge of interstellar society including its rules, history, art forms, codes of conduct and its important leaders. Educated people are expected to know about these kinds of things, whilst the unwashed masses, in their ignorance, might know only their local planet’s customs and nothing else.

cyber.name: Cyber
cyber.description: The Cyber Skill allows you to repair and modify robots, drones and cybernetic attachments. It also covers your skill in remotely piloting any drones you might own or be currently in control of.

medicine.name: Medicine
medicine.description: The Medicine Skill covers everything from patching up wounds to resuscitating a dying comrade. Characters with the Trained Doctor background can even attempt surgery, but should refrain from doing anything too ambitious until they get a good Skill level. Medicine can also be used to diagnose medical problems such as disease, poisoning and chemical intoxication. Provided suitable medical facilities are available most of these problems, once diagnosed, can be cured within a day or so.

planetaryKnowledge.name: Planetary Knowledge
planetaryKnowledge.description: This Skill represents your knowledge of different planets – their general location, their systems of government, and their general economy. Although most people rely on computers to give them facts about other worlds, restrictive modern copyright law means most interstellar encyclopedias are shockingly incomplete. Well-known systems such as Sol or Achenar are easy to recall, whereas obscure outer rim worlds are more difficult. This Skill ties in nicely with Navigation. Navigation tells you how to get to a new system; Planetary Knowledge tells you what is actually there.

science.name: Science
science.description: The Science Skill includes the three great sciences, physics, chemistry and biology. Science lets you understand how things work in the universe and can be used to predict the effects of an action. On a practical level you can use Science to understand how close you can fly to a turbulent planet or star, to calculate if your ship will still be able to take off on a heavy gravity world, or to estimate when that supernova is going to go critical. A good knowledge of science makes you look very smart, which can be helpful in some situations.

tactics.name: Tactics
tactics.description: Tactics is your ability to assess a situation quickly and determine the best course of action. It is mostly used to determine initiative in Combat, but it can also be used to spot good ambush areas or to predict the actions of an enemy commander on the battlefield.

trading.name: Trading
trading.description: Trading is the ability to understand and prosper in the complex trading environment of the Elite: Dangerous universe. This Skill is mostly used between adventures to gather extra income – a good Trading Skill and a large cargo hold can net a large amount of extra cash. You will use it in game to predict good trading routes and to judge whether the sale price of an item is fair or not.

bargain.name: Bargain
bargain.description: Bargain is your skill in getting what you want in some kind of exchange, usually involving money. You can use it with vendors and shop keepers to get cheaper equipment, and it can also be used to bribe people. The GM might allow you to use this Skill between adventures to get cheaper equipment.

bluff.name: Bluff
bluff.description: Bluff is your skill at lying, deception and disguise. Use it to convince people you are someone you are not or to play the innocent when the police turn up.

charm.name: Charm
charm.description: Charm is your ability to make people feel good about themselves and to trust you based on nothing more than your raw charisma. People who like you are less inclined to be suspicious of you or to want to harm you. It works well with other abilities such as Diplomacy, Bluff and Bargain.

diplomacy.name: Diplomacy
diplomacy.description: Diplomacy is the ability to resolve disputes through respect and persuasion, treating your debating target as an equal. Use it when you wish to show common cause with a potential enemy, or to explain, rationally, what you are doing, to a suspicious guard. Diplomacy relies on openness and honesty – if you are lying to your target use Bluff instead.

gambling.name: Gambling
gambling.description: With Gambling you increase your skill in all games of chance, from card games to token slot machines. You can count cards and figure out the win/loss conditions programmed into casino gambling machines.

insight.name: Insight
insight.description: The Insight Skill allows you to read people’s emotional state by studying their faces and body posture. It is not telepathy but it can tell you if a person is lying, earnest, angry, in love or intoxicated, making it very helpful during interrogations and questioning.

intimidate.name: Intimidate
intimidate.description: Intimidate lets you cajole, threaten and bully obedience into a person. It is a very aggressive form of communication but is sometimes the best way to shock an angry foe into submission.

streetwise.name: Streetwise
streetwise.description: Surviving in rough urban areas when you are a nice, middle class spaceship owner can be tough. Many street gangs use a vernacular that is hard to understand and follow a set of cultural mores that might not be consistent with society in general. In order to find information or discover where to buy rare, possibly illegal, items, you’ll need Streetwise to navigate your way through the shocking criminal underclass of the galaxy.

navigation.name: Navigation
navigation.description: Navigation covers all forms of orienteering, map reading and astro-navigation. You can plot a route through mountain ranges or nebula, figure out where you are if you become lost, and work out the most efficient routes in all kinds of terrain. Most Navigation is done with the aid of computers in the 34th century, but you are also able to navigate using stars and by identifying major landscape locations provided you have some knowledge of the planet you are on

repair.name: Repair
repair.description: Your Repair Skill allows you to fix all kinds of machinery, including spaceships and vehicles. While most pieces of technology have readable ‘fix-it’ guides downloadable from a chip inside the device or machine, Repair shows how handy you are around machines. It measures your skill and dexterity at using tools and the common sense required not to mess up the job and make things worse

shipPiloting.name: Spaceship Piloting
shipPiloting.description: This is your skill at flying spaceships. In addition to being used when you make any dangerous manoeuvres, such as skimming asteroids or flying down narrow canyons, it is primarily used in Spaceship Combat to determine the Defence of your ship.

shipWeapons.name: Spaceship Weapons
shipWeapons.description: Governs your ability to hit with weapons mounted on spaceships. This is used in Spaceship Combat.

systems.name: Systems
systems.description: This Skill allows you to operate scanner and sensor systems on a spaceship or ground based vehicle. It also allows you to activate and control the internal machinery inside a spaceship or vehicle, such as the airlocks and bulkheads, or any mining equipment like refineries or drones. Normally things like adjusting the temperature don’t require a Skill check, but sucking the air out of a passenger compartment or overloading the engines to explode might.

vehiclePiloting.name: Vehicle Piloting
vehiclePiloting.description: This is your ability to drive or pilot ground or underwater vehicles such as SRV’s or Subs. It is mostly used to determine your Defence in Vehicle Combat, but is also used when you try to pull off a very difficult manoeuvre such as performing a sharp turn or driving over a high ramp.

vehicleWeapons.name: Vehicle Weapons
vehicleWeapons.description: Governs your ability to hit with weapons mounted on vehicles. This is used in Vehicle Combat.

athletics.name: Athletics
athletics.description: Athletics represents your ability to jump, run, climb, swim and otherwise perform feats of physical prowess. It is also used to see how long you can hold your breath and how far you can run.

perception.name: Perception
perception.description: Perception covers the use of all five senses, sight, sound, touch, taste and smell. It is used to spot hidden items, detect ambushes, listen through closed doors and to identify a strange taste or smell. Spies and paranoid soldiers rely on a good perception to spot potential trouble before it strikes.

security.name: Security
security.description: Security is your understanding of locks, restraints, traps, observation cameras and any other device designed to keep you out of an area you are not supposed to be in. With a good Security you can override locked doors, unlock handcuffs, and predict when the next surveillance sweep is taking place in an enemy compound.

sleightOfHand.name: Sleight of Hand
sleightOfHand.description: Sleight of hand is the art of making small objects ‘disappear’, often into your pocket. It allows you to grab small items, no bigger than your hand, without anyone looking and place them anywhere you can reach. Unless you plan on becoming a stage magician this Skill is most commonly used by thieves to pinch stuff that doesn’t belong to them.

stealth.name: Stealth
stealth.description: Stealth covers both your ability to hide and to remain quiet. Sneaking around is a very useful Skill for spies and saboteurs, and indeed anyone who’d prefer to avoid combat.

survival.name: Survival
survival.description: This Skill covers the ability to survive in hostile natural environments. It is most useful on alien ‘earth-type’ worlds where it might be possible to scavenge for food and water, but at its most basic level it helps you find shelter, conserve your supplies and keep you alive long enough to be rescued. Those with a high Survival Skill might even be able to track people or animals through the wilderness.

sheet.cyberKarmaHint: Maximum cyber-only Karma (2 per Cyber enhancement)

sheet.skillUsedHint: Used this adventure — improves by 1 at the end of the adventure

sheet.equipmentComing: Arrives with the equipment item types.

escapeDeath.name: Escape Death
escapeDeath.description: Survive an attack that would have killed you or dropped your Endurance below 1. Your Karma points drop to zero.

sheet.clothingHint: Clothing and armour you have with you. Tick what you are wearing: worn clothing gives its Social Factor.
sheet.speedHint: Movement per turn: 10m, +2m per Quick Runner.

systemMaxBackgrounds.name: Maximum Background choices
systemMaxBackgrounds.hint: Specifies the maximum number of background choices. Default value is 4. 'Trained Pilot' is free and it is not included in the pool. 0 means unlimited choices

defaultDifficultyNumber.name: Default test difficulty number
defaultDifficultyNumber.hint: Specifies the default difficulty number for roll checks

allowToRerollAllTests.name: Allow to reroll all tests
allowToRerollAllTests.hint: Homerule - allows to reroll all tests using Karma point. Core Book rule allows to reroll only when there is a 1 on roll dice

socialFactorCap.name: Social Factor cap (house rule)
socialFactorCap.hint: Maximum positive Social Factor added to rolls. 0 = no cap, as in the Core Rules.

explosiveMode.name: Explosives: battle map
explosiveMode.hint: Grenades and missiles work differently with and without a map (Core Rules pp.58–60): the grenade difficulty, where a miss lands, and who is caught. "Ask" lets the attacker choose each time; cards without a choice offer both.

vehicleTurnPanel.name: Spaceship and vehicle turn panel
vehicleTurnPanel.hint: When a ship or vehicle's turn starts, the GM and its owners get a panel that steps through the turn in the book's order (Adjust Speed, Equipment, Recharge Shields, Check for Obstacles, Combat Action), then ends the turn. Shields recharge at their own step, after Equipment. Off: shields recharge at the start of the turn and everything is done from the sheet.

silentRunningRounds.name: Silent Running: rounds per minute
silentRunningRounds.hint: A ship can run silent for a minute before it overheats (Core Rules p.268), but the book never says how long a combat round lasts. Its overheating damage comes every ten seconds, so by default a round is ten seconds: six rounds to a minute. Each Heat Sink fired adds another minute.

item.choicesHint: Some backgrounds (e.g. Army Trained) take two choices.
item.freeHint: Does not count towards the character's limit.
item.costAllHint: Spends the whole Karma pool and can't be used at 0 (Escape Death).
item.skillModsWeaponHint: Applied while the weapon is equipped (e.g. +10 Parry for a Neo-Samurai Sword).
item.skillModsArmourHint: Applied while the armour is worn (e.g. Riot Armour −20 Athletics).
item.boostHint: Offered on the attack card: an attack bonus while your attack misses, a defence bonus while an attack against you hits.
item.grantsHint: Added from the Enhancements compendium when this background is added to a character, and removed with it.
item.requiresHint: Any one of these backgrounds, separated by commas.
item.rollBonusesHint: "Always" bonuses are added to every check with that Skill; the others are offered as tick boxes in the check dialog (Medpacks are ticked for Stabilise and Treat wounds). A Skill score bonus counts only if it lifts your Skill bonus.
item.skillModsWornHint: Applied while worn (clothing) or installed (cybernetics), e.g. Cybernetic Eyes +5 Perception.

skillConfig.title: Skill
skillConfig.learningHint: Permanent improvements: independent learning at creation, rank-up D10s and +1 from each ticked adventure.
skillConfig.capBonusHint: Rank Skill Cap is {cap}. Natural Genius raises one skill's cap by 10.
skillConfig.modHint: Added to the score after the Skill Cap; the score can never exceed 100.

socialFactor.title: Social Factor
socialFactor.hint: Added to Bargain, Bluff, Charm and Diplomacy rolls (not to the Skill score). The GM can rule it doesn't apply to a particular roll.
socialFactor.wornHint: Social Factor of clothing and other items (e.g. Tailored Business Suit +1, wrist com −2). Worn armour is added automatically.
socialFactor.damagedHint: You lose any positive Social Factor from clothing once you take damage. Ticked automatically when Endurance drops; untick after changing clothes.
socialFactor.cosmeticsHint: Only one cosmetics bonus applies at a time. Refusing to use cosmetics is −1.
socialFactor.otherHint: Any other adjustment the GM allows.
socialFactor.cyborgHint: Non-discreet or revealed cybernetics: Social Factor is −3 and nothing else alters it.
socialFactor.confidentHint: No Social Factor penalties from equipment, armour or cybernetics.

endAdventure.title: End of Adventure
endAdventure.buttonHint: Ticked skills gain +1 (unless that would exceed the Skill Cap) and all ticks are cleared. Optionally restores Karma for the next adventure.
endAdventure.atCap: At Skill Cap — tick cleared, no improvement
endAdventure.ticksCleared: All skill ticks will be cleared.
endAdventure.restoreKarma: Restore all Karma for the next adventure ({value} / {max})

contest.opponentBonusHint: For opponents without the skill listed, e.g. their Perception or To Hit from the stat block.

ties.initiator: Ties: the acting character (opponent's roll sets the difficulty)

pairs.stealth: Core Rules p.267: the searcher's Perception check is the number your Stealth must pass.
pairs.charm: Core Rules p.33 (Seduce): Charm against the target's Insight check.
pairs.athletics: Core Rules p.61 (Grab/Escape): you must beat the opponent's Athletics; ties go to them.

contest.needsGM: A GM must be logged in to update this contest.

tiesShort.initiator: Ties go to the acting character

karma.useHint: Spend the Karma and post the effect to chat.
karma.usedHint: Already used this turn; you get it back at the start of your next turn.
karma.usedThisTurn: {name} has already been used this turn.
karma.restHint: Main rest (a full night's sleep): regain 1 Karma point.
karma.usedThisBattle: {name} has already been used this battle.
karma.usesLeft: Opponent capability — {left} of {max} uses left this battle

damage.title: Damage
damage.explosiveKnock: Everyone caught in the blast is knocked over, unless the GM rules otherwise.
damage.knock: A 10 on the damage dice: the target is knocked over.
damage.noKnockEnergy: A 10 was rolled, but Energy weapons have no concussive force: no knockdown.
damage.applySelectedHint: Select the tokens that were hit (e.g. everyone in the blast radius, or within 6m for divided fire).
damage.noneSelected: Select the tokens to apply the damage to first.
damage.escapeDeathHint: Spend all your Karma to avoid the attack that just dropped you below 1 Endurance.

bleed.odd: {name} rolls {roll}: loses {loss} Endurance, an odd number — stabilised.
bleed.even: {name} rolls {roll}: loses {loss} Endurance, an even number — still bleeding.
bleed.cauterised: {name} rolls {roll}: the Energy wound is cauterised — stabilised, no further damage.
bleed.cauterisedTen: {name} rolls a 10: the internal damage is too severe — loses {loss} Endurance and keeps bleeding.

damage.noMedic: Select the token of the character giving aid (or set your user character) first.
damage.deathAtHint: Below 0 Endurance a character bleeds out; at a negative score of half maximum Endurance they die.
damage.bleedOutHint: Lose a D10 Endurance: odd stabilises, even keeps bleeding. Rolled automatically at the start of the turn in combat.
damage.stabiliseHint: An ally's Medicine check (select their token): difficulty 8 if dropped by an Energy weapon, 10 otherwise.
damage.treatHint: Medicine check with a Medpack or proper kit, at most every six hours: heals the check's total. Select the medic's token to have someone else treat.
damage.disarm: Even number on the Fighting die: a weapon or item is knocked out of the target's hands (the GM picks where).
damage.freeKnock: It was a free attack: their turn ends.
damage.aimHint: Spend your turn aiming at one enemy for +5 To Hit next turn. Lost if you take damage, are attacked in close combat, or lose sight of them.
damage.vengeful: Vengeful: {name} is down to single-digit Endurance and can immediately attack {attacker} (if in range of a held weapon and in sight). {attacker} then resumes their turn.
damage.molten: Molten munitions: {dice}D10 Energy damage at the start of the target's next turn.
damage.moltenApplied: Splashed with molten metal: {dice}D10 Energy damage at the start of their next turn.
damage.destroysArmourNote: Anti-Material Projector: armour gives no protection, and a hit destroys it.
damage.doubleRobot: Double damage against a robot or drone.

weapon.attackBonusHint: A rare weapon's bonus to the attacker's Skill score, used only when attacking with this weapon (never above 100).
weapon.damageHint: Damage is a roll formula (1d10, 3d10, 8). Burst adds damage for each point the attack beats the difficulty, up to the maximum.
weapon.reload: Reload (a fresh magazine; leftover rounds are lost)
weapon.equippedHint: In hand: its skill modifiers apply
weapon.rollHint: Roll an attack ({skill}). Shift-click to skip the dialog.
weapon.rollOpponent: Roll an attack with this weapon
weapon.reloadedNoSpare: {weapon} reloaded (no spare ammunition carried for it).

armour.hint: Absorbs damage of the listed types; every hit still does at least 1 damage, except Toxic. Hardened N: roll a D10, and on N or more the protection is doubled. Discreet armour worn under clothes has no Social Factor penalty.
armour.destroyedHint: Destroyed by an Anti-Material Projector: gives no protection until repaired.

combat.protectionHint: Armour absorbs damage of its types; every hit still does at least 1 damage, except Toxic. Hardened: on a D10 of that number or more the protection is doubled.
combat.karmaHint: Personal and Any Combat capabilities, for quick use in a fight.

opponent.fightingLine: Finesse 5, +{toHit} To Hit, Damage 1D10 halved (Fighting is To Hit −1 unless listed)
opponent.karmaHint: Opponents have no Karma points: each capability can be used once per battle.
opponent.roboticHint: Robots and drones: immune to Toxic damage, and take double damage from Anti-Material Projectors.

attack.title: Attack: {weapon}
attack.noAmmo: {weapon} is out of ammo — reload first.
attack.noTarget: No target selected: enter the target's Defence below, or target a token first.
attack.squaresHint: Difficulty is 7 or the number of squares, whichever is greater.
attack.groundTargetHint: For explosives aimed at a patch of ground or a wall rather than at an enemy.
attack.coverHint: Behind boxes, a tree or other people. Ranged attacks only.
attack.defenceHint: Melee and Fighting attacks can be Dodged or Parried; the GM chooses for opponents.
attack.aimHint: Aimed at this enemy for a whole turn and kept the aim.
attack.knockedOverHint: Adds no skill bonus to the attack.
attack.divideFireHint: Hits everyone within 6m of the target (at least 8m away) on the same roll; damage is halved.
attack.adjustHint: Anything else the GM rules (e.g. darkness, smoke).
attack.cantEvade: The target can't evade: only the weapon's difficulty counts.
attack.divideFireNote: Divided fire: also checks everyone within 6m of the target; halve the damage.
attack.destroyCoverNote: If it missed only because of cover, the cover is destroyed (unless very tough).
attack.explosiveNote: Explosion: Fatal and Injury radii take their damage; everyone caught is knocked over unless the GM rules otherwise.
attack.boostHint: Spend the Karma and add this to the attack you just made.
attack.defenceBoostHint: {name}: spend the Karma and add this to your Defence against this attack.
attack.throwWithHint: With advantage: round a corner, down stairs, somewhere you can duck into cover. With disadvantage: bowled in an open fire-fight.
attack.freeHint: An adjacent enemy moved away or shot at point blank range. If this knocks them over, their turn ends.
attack.grabHint: Only someone roughly your size or smaller. On a hit, an opposed Athletics check (plus Strength damage bonuses) decides it.
attack.counterHint: You Parried and the attack missed: make an immediate Melee or Fighting attack (it doesn't use your next action).
attack.counterIntro: Counter-attack: the enemy can't counter this if it misses.
attack.counterMissNote: A missed counter-attack can't be countered (except with Riposte).
attack.riposteHint: Spend the Karma to counter-attack the counter-attack that just missed you.

background.chooseEnhancements: {name}: choose {count} Enhancement(s) from the Enhancements compendium.

hint.ambidextrous: Automated: the two-weapon penalty on attacks becomes −1, then 0.
hint.awareness: Automated: Initiative uses the better of your Tactics and Perception bonuses.
hint.confident: Automated: Social Factor ignores penalties from equipment, armour and cybernetics.
hint.dynamicKarma: Not automated: remember to pay only for the most expensive capability.
hint.hardToKill: Automated: death at minus maximum Endurance; twice, Escape Death costs at most 4 Karma.
hint.naturalGenius: Automated: +10 to the chosen Skill's Skill Cap (max 100).
hint.quickRunner: Automated: +2m Speed each time (up to three times).
hint.strong: Automated: +2 Fighting and Melee damage each time (max +10).
hint.tough: Automated: +5 maximum Endurance each time (up to 80).
hint.overclocking: Engineering improvements without faults on new ships (Repair 40/50/70 → 1/2/3). Applied by hand until ship engineering is added.
hint.survivalist: The skill check dialog offers your Survival bonus as an extra (unticked) bonus on non-combat checks.
hint.vengeful: Damage cards flag when an enemy attack drops you to 1–9 Endurance, so you can attack back at once.

creation.title: Character creation
creation.finishIncomplete: Only {done} of {total} steps are done. Finish creation anyway? (Endurance and Karma will be filled to their maximums and this checklist hidden.)
creation.overCap: Above the Skill Cap of {cap}: {skills}. Lower a background bonus or pick a different Skill.
creation.learningHint: Pick ten Skills to improve: +10 to the first, +9 to the second … +1 to the tenth. The number after each Skill is its score before these points; no Skill may go above {cap}.

hint.backgrounds: Four choices; two-choice backgrounds such as Army Trained use two. Pilot Trained is free and already on the sheet.
hint.openSkills: Self-Taught and University Graduate have skill lines for you to choose: open the background and pick the Skills.
hint.enhancements: Gene Mod Baby and Self-Taught let you choose Enhancements: drag them from the Enhancements compendium.
hint.karma: Pick three from the Karma Capabilities compendium. Escape Death is free and doesn't count.
hint.equipment: One or two Autopistols or Laser Pistols (two spare clips for Autopistols), Flight Suit, Magboots, Remlok, a hand-held or wrist com, 1000 credits; a knife, sword or sledgehammer with Melee Weapons 20+, a Fragmentation grenade with Grenade 20+. On the ship: a Spacesuit, a Medpack and a basic Spaceship Repair Kit.
hint.ship: Choose one of the eight starting ships, or build one with up to 100,000 credits (unspent credits are lost).
hint.finish: Finishing fills Endurance and Karma to their maximums and hides this checklist.
hint.partnerBackgrounds: Three choices for a partner; Pilot Trained isn't free but can be one of them.
hint.partnerEquipment: The same personal equipment as a character (pistol, Flight Suit, Magnetic Boots, Remlok, com, a melee weapon or grenade at 20+), but no ship.

creation.equipmentIntro: Adds the starting kit from the compendia and 1000 credits. You can't spend money until the game starts unless the GM says otherwise.
creation.partnerEquipmentIntro: Adds the personal starting kit from the compendia. Partners don't get a ship or its equipment.

gear.activeHint: In use: its Social Factor counts (a com on show, cosmetics applied, a gas mask on).
gear.hint: Bonuses apply while carried. Ammunition is used up when you reload a weapon whose name (or compendium group) contains the text above.
gear.powerHint: While switched on (In use), each of the wearer's turns uses a round of power; at 0 the device switches off until a new battery or Alien Power Cell is fitted. A healing device restores its Endurance at the start of the wearer's turn.
gear.drained: Out of power: it switches off.

cybernetic.karmaHint: Cybernetics drain Karma permanently, from cybernetic Karma (Cybernetic Affinity) first. Upgrading a device you already have costs no Karma: set the new one's cost to 0.
cybernetic.karmaSummary: Karma drained: {spent} from your Karma maximum, {fromCyber} from cybernetic Karma.
cybernetic.cyborgNote: Cybernetics show (or are revealed): Social Factor is fixed at −3.

clothing.hint: Worn clothing gives its Social Factor (positive values are lost once you take damage) and its Skill modifiers.

hint.mapped: D10 for the direction from the target square (1–8 clockwise from the square above it; 9–10 overshoots along the line of fire), then D10 squares.
hint.mapless: Roll on the Grenade or Missile Miss Table.
hint.caught: If the GM is unsure how many people are in the blast: roll a D10 and halve it.

scatter.mappedOvershoot: Scatter {roll}: overshoots — it carries on {squares} squares ({metres}m) past the target square along the line from you, stopping at a wall or solid obstacle, then explodes.

grenade.short: Rubbish throw! It slips from your grasp and rolls only {metres} metres forward before exploding.
grenade.whoosh: Whoosh! Complete miss: it explodes where it injures no one (the GM may rule it damages equipment).
grenade.long: Too long! It lands {metres} metres beyond the target point, or against the back wall.
grenade.random: What the…? It bounces off walls and ceilings and lands at the feet of a random person, chosen by the GM.

missile.whoosh: Whoosh! Complete miss: it explodes where it injures no one (the GM may rule it damages equipment).
missile.long: Too long! It lands {metres} metres beyond the target point, or against the back wall.
missile.short: Ooops! It lands {metres} metres short of the target point, possibly with you in the blast.

scatter.caughtResult: Caught in the blast: D10 {roll}, halved — {people} (the GM decides who is in the fatal or injury radius).

modeNote.mapless: Explosives without a map: the GM decides who is in each radius.

grab.resolveHint: Both roll Athletics plus Strength damage bonuses (opponents may use To Hit); you must beat the target.
grab.success: grabbed! Both have Dodge 0 and can't Parry; the target can only try to escape.
grab.escapeHint: Your action: Athletics (+ Strength) against the grabber's; you must exceed it.
grab.escaped: Escaped! You can still move, and the grabber gets no free attack.

stim.title: Stim injector
stim.injectHint: Inject a carried Combat Stim (needs a syringe or injector). Unconscious characters wake, knocked over.
stim.endsHint: After about an hour. At 0 Endurance or less you fall unconscious.
stim.noInjector: You need a syringe or Stim injector to apply it.
stim.injected: {injector}: rolled {roll} (needed {chance} or less) — {drug} injected; {name} stays conscious.
stim.failed: {injector}: rolled {roll} (needed {chance} or less) — no injection; it tries again at the end of each of {name}'s turns.
stim.overload: {injector}: rolled 100 — the stimulant overloads {name}'s heart. Dead.

rankUp.title: Rank up: {rank}
rankUp.banner: New rank reached: {rank} (Skill Cap {cap}). Apply the rank-up to improve ten Skills and choose a Karma Capability or Enhancement.
rankUp.more: ({count} ranks to apply, one at a time.)
rankUp.choiceEnhancement: A new Enhancement (instead of a Karma Capability)
rankUp.skillsHint: Choose ten different Skills; each gains a D10, but none can go above the new Skill Cap ({cap}). The number shown is the current score.
rankUp.pickTen: Choose {count} Skills (fewer only if no other Skill has room under the cap).
rankUp.pickKarma: {name}: drag a new Karma Capability from the compendium onto the sheet.
rankUp.pickEnhancement: {name}: drag a new Enhancement from the compendium onto the sheet.
rankUp.partnerNote: A partner rolls ten Skills and gains 5 Endurance, but no Karma point, Karma Capability or Enhancement.
rankUp.partnerChoice: No new Karma Capability or Enhancement (partner)

partner.tooDeep: The third partner in a chain can't have a partner of their own (they would start off dead).
partner.noKarmaItems: Partners have no Karma Capabilities of their own: they use their host's.
partner.backgroundLimit: Partners have {limit} background choices (Pilot Trained uses one).
partner.noHost: {name} has no host character to draw Karma from.
partner.hostRefuses: {host} doesn't let their partner spend their Karma.
partner.visibleCybernetics: {name} has visible cybernetics and can no longer use {host}'s Karma.
partner.notHostOwner: You need permission on {host} to spend their Karma.
partner.confirmUnknown: Can {name} see {host}, within {range}m? (Their tokens aren't both on this scene.)
partner.confirmFar: {name} is {distance}m from {host} — more than {range}m. Use the Karma anyway (e.g. the GM allows it)?
partner.virtualKarma: Cybernetics: {cost} of {total} virtual Karma (the host's total)
partner.rankHint: A partner's rank follows the host's Rank Points.
partner.ranksUp: {name} (a partner) has a rank-up to apply.
partner.allowKarma: My partner may spend my Karma
partner.allowKarmaHint: A partner who can see you within 30m can use your Karma Capabilities, paid from your Karma (Core Rules p.27).
partner.depth3: (third in the chain: Endurance −15; can't have a partner)

craft.weaponHint: Burst weapons add 5 damage for each point the attack beats the target's Defence, up to the maximum. Kinetic weapons typically add +5 against Hull, energy weapons +5 against Shields; missiles list lower damage against Shields.

vehicle.pilotHint: Drag a character or opponent onto the sheet, or choose one here. Their Vehicle Piloting gives Defence and Pursuit, Tactics gives Initiative, and Vehicle Weapons fires the fixed and gimballed weapons.
vehicle.defenceHint: Agility + the pilot's Vehicle Piloting bonus + the Speed Table bonus. 0 when stationary.
vehicle.pursuitHint: Current Speed + half the pilot's Vehicle Piloting bonus (rounded down).
vehicle.shieldsDownHint: Knocked-out shields charge up by their recharge each turn and work again once back to half their maximum.
vehicle.zoneFromMap: (from the token's position on the combat map)
vehicle.setSpeedHint: Set the current speed (click again to stop)
vehicle.noTarget: No vehicle targeted: type the target's Defence.
vehicle.targetDefenceHint: 0 if the target is stationary or sniping.
vehicle.naturalTen: Natural 10: against a spaceship this would also hit a component (vehicles take no critical hits).
vehicle.selectVehicles: Select the vehicle tokens to damage first.

scenes.imported: The Vehicle and Space Combat Map scenes have been added to the "{folder}" scene folder.

vcombat.turnOrder: Adjust speed → equipment → shields → obstacles → action
vcombat.speedRange: Speed {speed}; this turn it can be set from {min} to {max}.
vcombat.speedRangeHint: Your Accelerate and Decelerate ratings limit how far your speed can change this turn. Once chosen, you keep it for the whole round.
vcombat.speedLimit: This turn your speed can only be set from {min} to {max}.
vcombat.speedLocked: Your speed is fixed until your next turn.
vcombat.speedLockedHint: In combat you can only change speed at the start of your own turn.
vcombat.startTurnHint: Start this vehicle's turn now (normally automatic when the combat tracker reaches it).
vcombat.clearHint: Clear combat states (fleeing, sniping, rammed, speed lock…).
vcombat.escaped: {name} has fled and escapes the battlefield.
vcombat.noOneUpClose: No enemies are up-close, so {name} moves at-distance.
vcombat.shieldsBack: Shields charged to {value} and back online.
vcombat.stationary: {name} is stationary: no obstacle check needed.
vcombat.resultHint: Roll on the table, or pick the result yourself.

obstacleText.rough: Rocks, crowds or boulders ahead. Vehicle Piloting check (+ Agility) at twice the speed, or take 5 Damage per speed point and lose the action.
obstacleText.large: A huge immovable obstacle ahead. Vehicle Piloting check (+ Agility) at twice the speed, or take 10 Damage per speed point, stop dead and lose the action.
obstacleText.slope: A steep slope the vehicle is forced to drive over.

slope.safe: Speed {speed} is safe at this gravity (up to {safe}): no check needed.
slope.risky: Speed {speed} is risky (up to {risky}): Difficulty 8 Vehicle Piloting check, or lose the action sailing through the air.
slope.auto: Speed {speed} is too fast: the vehicle is launched into the air. Difficulty 12 check to control the descent or take {damage} Damage; the action is lost either way.

fail.roughOk: The pilot swerves aside and can still act.
fail.rough: The vehicle smashes through at Speed {speed}: {damage} Damage.
fail.large: The vehicle smashes into the obstruction at Speed {speed}: {damage} Damage, and it stops dead.
fail.slopeOk: The vehicle bounces back to earth with no problems.
fail.slope: The vehicle sails through the air and lands safely.
fail.slopeAutoOk: The thrusters slow the descent: a safe landing.

vcombat.noTarget: No vehicle on this scene can be targeted.
vcombat.noTargetUpClose: No vehicle up-close can be targeted.
vcombat.noTurrets: {name} has no turrets to fire broadsides.
vcombat.lostActionConfirm: {name} lost its action this turn (obstacle or slope). Take an action anyway?
vcombat.snipingTarget: The target is Sniping: an automatic hit.

actionHint.joust: Fire all weapons at a target in either zone, then move up-close (a Sniping target comes too). Jousting a Fleeing vehicle starts a Pursuit.
actionHint.snipe: Stop and fire all weapons at +1 To Hit. Your Defence is 0 until your next turn.
actionHint.strafe: Fire weapons one at a time until one misses, then move up-close and Disengage. Not against a Fleeing or Disengaging target.
actionHint.chicken: Charge a target with lower Pursuit; you both secretly choose impact or evade.
actionHint.flee: Escape at the start of your next turn, unless an enemy Jousts you and wins a Pursuit.
actionHint.pass: Hold position: one re-roll available until the end of your next turn.
actionHint.tail: D10 + Defence against the target's: the winner fires everything, the loser one turret. Tailing a Disengaging vehicle starts a Pursuit.
actionHint.broadsides: Fire your turrets at an up-close target until one misses.
actionHint.ram: D10 + Defence against the target's Defence or Pursuit. A hit deals 10 Damage per speed point (half to you); a tie sideswipes for 5 per speed point each.
actionHint.disengage: Move at-distance at the start of your next turn unless an enemy Tails you and wins a Pursuit. No attack.
actionHint.rescue: Stop (Speed 0) beside a wreck and pick up its stranded crew.
actionHint.dogfight: D10 + Defence against the target's: whoever gets behind fires everything, the other one turret. Dogfighting a Disengaging ship starts a Pursuit.
actionHint.faOff: Fire at an up-close target, weapon after weapon, until one misses. No Agility in your Defence until your next turn.
actionHint.hover: Combined combat: come to a halt over vehicles and people. Fixed and gimballed weapons fire at one target; each turret can pick its own. Your Defence is 0 until your next action.
actionHint.crawl: Combined combat: at Speed 0, stay up-close and fire all weapons at one person.

actionText.snipe: {name} stops dead and snipes at {target}. Its Defence is 0 until its next turn.
actionText.flee: {name} turns to flee. It escapes at the start of its next turn unless Jousted and caught.
actionText.pass: {name} holds position and assesses. One re-roll is available until the end of its next turn.
actionText.broadsides: {name} steadies to fire its turrets at {target}.
actionText.disengage: {name} pulls away to disengage. It reaches at-distance at the start of its next turn unless Tailed and caught.
actionText.rescue: {name} stops to pick up stranded crew.
actionText.faOff: {name} switches Flight Assist off to line up on {target}. No Agility in its Defence until its next turn.
actionText.hover: {name} hovers over the battlefield, guns trained on {target}. Its Defence is 0 until its next action.
actionText.crawl: {name} slows to a crawl and turns every weapon on {target}.

vcombat.broadsidesLeft: Missed. The remaining turrets ({weapons}) must pick a different up-close target; fire them from the sheet.

flee.chaser: {chaser} catches up: it attacks, both move up-close and {runner} stops fleeing.
flee.tie: Neither gains: both stay at-distance and nobody fires.

disengage.chaser: {chaser} stays on its tail: {runner} stops disengaging and is attacked.
disengage.tie: Neither gains: both move at-distance and nobody fires.

vcombat.tailDraw: {name} and {target} circle each other. Each may fire a single turret.
vcombat.tailReturn: {name} can fire back with a single turret.
vcombat.chickenPursuit: Chicken needs a higher Pursuit than the target ({mine} vs {theirs} for {target}).
vcombat.chickenChoose: {name} charges {target}. Impact or evade? Your choice stays secret until they choose.
vcombat.chickenWaiting: {name} charges {target}! {target}'s controller must choose: impact or evade.
vcombat.chickenSecret: The attacker's choice is hidden until the target chooses.
vcombat.chickenEven: Both evade. The die shows {roll} (even): head-on collision!
vcombat.chickenOdd: Both evade. The die shows {roll} (odd): {name} swoops around behind.
vcombat.chickenTail: {name} forces {target} to spin out and tries to get on its tail (+2).
vcombat.collisionText: Each vehicle takes {damage} Damage (5 × their combined speed) and both stop dead.
vcombat.forwardRamChicken: {name}'s Forward Ram halves the Damage it takes.

ram.hit: {name} rams {target} for {damage} Damage and takes {self} itself.
ram.sideswipe: A sideswipe: both vehicles take {damage} Damage.
ram.bomb: {name} rams {target} for {damage} Damage and explodes, destroying itself.

vcombat.forwardRam: Forward Ram: the rammer takes no Damage.
vcombat.rammedNote: A vehicle damaged by a Ram can't add its Agility to Defence until its next turn starts.
vcombat.forwardRamHint: Takes no Damage when its Ram hits, and half Damage from a Chicken collision.

stateHint.escaped: Fled the battlefield. The GM decides what happens next.
stateHint.fleeing: Escapes at the start of its next turn unless Jousted and caught.
stateHint.disengaging: Reaches at-distance at the start of its next turn unless Tailed and caught.
stateHint.sniping: Defence 0 until its next turn: anyone firing at it hits automatically.
stateHint.rammed: Damaged by a Ram: no Agility in Defence until its next turn.
stateHint.lostAction: Lost this turn's action to an obstacle or slope.
stateHint.pass: Passed: one re-roll available until the end of its next turn.

drone.title: Drone
drone.enabledHint: No crew: uses the fixed Defence, Initiative and Pursuit below; each weapon's Accuracy holds its listed To Hit.
drone.flyingHint: Flies: makes no obstacle checks, and fixed-mount vehicle weapons can't target it.
drone.defenceHint: Plus the Speed Table's Defence bonus; 0 when stationary.
drone.bombHint: Extra Damage when its Ram or Chicken connects (the second figure if the target's shields are still up). It is destroyed doing so. 0 = not a bomb.
drone.bombShields: {name} explodes against the shields for {damage} extra Damage.
drone.fixedVsFlying: {weapon} is a fixed mount and can't target {target}, which is flying.
drone.flyingNoObstaclesPlain: {name} is flying and makes no obstacle checks.
drone.controlledBy: Controlled by {name} (Cyber +{bonus} to To Hit and Dodge)
drone.dropController: Robotic: drop the controlling character here to add their Cyber skill bonus.

vdestroy.title: {name} is destroyed
vdestroy.crew: Caught in the wreck: {crew}. Player characters take 4D10 Endurance Damage; other crew generally go down with the vehicle (GM's call).
vdestroy.rescueHint: Survivors are stranded until another vehicle stops (Speed 0) and takes the Rescue action.
vdestroy.chipHint: Hull 0 or less. Raise the Hull to repair it.
vdestroy.strandedHint: Crew waiting at the wreck to be picked up.
vdestroy.noStranded: Nobody on this scene is waiting to be rescued.
vdestroy.mustStop: {name} must slow to Speed 0 to pick anyone up.
vdestroy.whoToRescue: Who do you pick up from the wreck of {wreck}?
vdestroy.rescued: {name} stops and picks up {crew} from the wreck of {wreck}.

ship.npcHint: For GM ships (Core Rules p.302 on): fixed Defence, Dogfighting, Pursuit and Initiative, no crew; each weapon's Accuracy holds its listed To Hit.
ship.dogfightingHint: Used instead of Defence in Dogfight rolls.
ship.criticalHint: The strength assumed for any component a critical hit strikes that the roster doesn't list (GM ships use it for every component).
ship.glance: The ships glance off each other: both take 5 Damage.
ship.spinsOut: {name} spins out of control: it can't start a Dogfight in its next turn.
ship.outOfControl: {name} is out of control and can't start a Dogfight this turn.
ship.outOfControlNote: {name} is out of control: no Dogfight this turn.
ship.outOfControlHint: Rammed by a ship its size or larger: it can't start a Dogfight this turn.
ship.faOffHint: Flight Assist off: no Agility in Defence until its next turn.
ship.collisionText: Head-on: {target} takes {a} Damage and {name} takes {b} (by the other ship's size).
ship.noFsd: {name}'s Frame Shift Drive is destroyed: it can't flee.
ship.noRecharge: The Power Distributor is destroyed: no shield recharge.
ship.immobilised: {name} is immobilised and can't take combat actions (it can still fire one turret from the sheet).
ship.immobilisedNote: {name} is immobilised: Defence 0 and no combat actions.
ship.destroyedAboard: Anyone still aboard is killed. The pilot can try an emergency eject (Systems, Difficulty 12); otherwise only Escape Death saves them. Crew outside the cockpit survive only with Escape Death.
ship.cargoScatter: {count} cargo canisters ({formula}) scatter intact, up to the cargo carried.
ship.defenceHint: Agility + the pilot's Spaceship Piloting bonus. 0 when immobilised or Sniping; no Agility with Flight Assist off.
ship.pursuitHint: Speed + half the pilot's Spaceship Piloting bonus (rounded down).
ship.componentsHint: In ship-roster order: critical hits on Utility Mounts and Internal Components count along this list. Fixed components a critical hit names but that aren't listed are added at the Critical value's strength.
ship.bonusesHint: From the ship roster's Bonuses line (Agility and Speed are already in the ship's ratings).

crit.naturalTen: Natural 10: a critical hit if the target's shields are down.
crit.nothing: Critical hit (D10 {roll}: {kind}): nothing there to hit. Re-roll, or the GM chooses the component.
crit.aimHint: Shields down, both up-close, gimballed weapon: the target gains +4 Defence and all the Damage goes to the component, not the Hull.
crit.weaponOut: {weapon} has been destroyed by a critical hit.

effect.powerPlant: Only emergency power: the ship can't move or fire and is immobilised.
effect.thrusters: The ship is immobilised: no combat actions, and only one turret can fire.
effect.fsd: No Frame Shift Drive: the ship can't flee, enter Supercruise or jump.
effect.lifeSupport: The canopy shatters: anyone in the cockpit without a Remlok or spacesuit is killed, and anyone not in magboots or strapped in is blown out into space.
effect.powerDistributor: −1 Agility and To Hit (−2 for GM ships), and the shields can't recharge.
effect.sensors: −1 Defence: the pilot can't see all the threats.
effect.shieldGenerator: The shields go down and stay down.
effect.weapon: The weapon can no longer fire.
effect.internal: The component stops working; its bonuses are lost.

equip.title: Equipment
equip.floatingIntro: Assign up to {n}, no more than one per area.
equip.floatingHint: From an advanced Power Distributor: each can go on engines (+1 Agility), weapons (+1 To Hit) or shields (+5 recharge), one per area. They stay until changed.
equip.chaffHint: Equipment Action: until your next turn, gimballed weapons and automatic turrets suffer −4 To Hit against you (+4 Defence). One ammo per use.
equip.minesHint: Equipment Action: until your next turn, anyone Dogfighting you must beat the launcher's Difficulty or lose and hit a mine. One ammo per use.
equip.pdHint: Automatic: when a missile, torpedo or mine would hit you, roll a D10; on an even score it is destroyed. One ammo per roll.
equip.ecmHint: +4 Defence against Seeker Missiles (not dumbfire missiles or torpedoes).
equip.bankHint: Equipment Action: one bank at a time adds its recharge boost now and for the rest of its rounds. Three uses per bank.
equip.rechargeHint: Shield recharge this turn, with floating bonuses and any running Shield Cell Bank.
equip.chaffNote: Chaff: +4 Defence against gimballed weapons and automatic turrets.
equip.chaffUsed: {name} fires chaff: gimballed weapons and automatic turrets suffer −4 against it until its next turn ({left}/{max} left).
equip.minesUsed: {name} lays mines: anyone Dogfighting it must beat {dn} until its next turn ({left}/{max} left).
equip.bankBusy: {name} already has a Shield Cell Bank running.
equip.noBank: {name} has no working Shield Cell Bank with uses left.
equip.bankUsed: {name} fires {bank}: +{boost} recharge for {rounds} round(s). Shields {before} → {after} ({uses} uses left).
equip.bankRunning: Shield Cell Bank running: {rounds} more round(s).
equip.bankDone: The Shield Cell Bank is spent.
equip.minesHit: {name} doesn't beat the minefield's {dn}: it loses the Dogfight and hits a mine.
equip.bankArmed: {bank} activated: +{boost} to this turn's Shield Recharge and the next ones ({rounds} in all). {uses} uses left.

shield.title: Personal Shield
shield.hint: While switched on (In use), the shield takes damage of the ticked types before armour, like a ship's shields; anything left over carries through. At the start of the wearer's turn it recharges, and once knocked down it charges back up to half strength before it holds again.

destab.label: Destabilisation Beam
destab.hint: A hit collapses the target's shields and puts the Damage straight on the Hull; a ship also takes it on every Fixed and Internal component (and its weapons and utility mounts on a critical hit); a vehicle that survives is disabled.
destab.collapse: Destabilisation Beam: the shields collapse and the Damage goes straight to the Hull.
destab.disabled: The vehicle is disabled: all its systems, weapons, scanners and engines fail, and take weeks to repair.

engineering.title: Engineering: {name}
engineering.overclock: Overclocking (new ship: pick a positive effect, no fault)
engineering.hint: Roll D10 + Repair bonus on the component's Engineering Table. A professional engineer rolls twice and you choose. It costs 50% of the component's base price; once engineered, a component can't be modified again.
engineering.againWarning: {name} has already been engineered, and a component can only be modified once. Engineer it again anyway?
engineering.overclockHint: Overclocking (Espionage Supplement): on a new ship, Repair 40 gives one improvement, 50 two and 70 three. Choose a positive effect from this component's table; it suffers no fault.

effect.accurate: Accurate (+1 To Hit for all weapons)
effect.extraCells: Extra Cells (+2 Shield Cell Bank duration)
effect.magnified: Magnified (one grade higher; A-grade or ungraded mounts become A*)
effect.tightGrapple: Tight Grapple (+1 Spaceship Piloting to interdict)
effect.wideGrapple: Wide Grapple (interdict one size larger, or +2 if already large)

engineering.chooseHint: The engineer rolled twice: choose the result you prefer.
engineering.costNote: Engineering costs 50% of the component's base price; restoring it costs 25%. Effects the system doesn't model (power, range, scans, mining) are recorded on the component.
engineering.malfunctionDone: Malfunction: the engineering failed, but the component was reset to normal.
engineering.bulkheadHardened: Bulkhead: Hull bonus doubled (adjust the Hull to match).
engineering.sparks: {name} sparks violently and drops to 0 Strength ({fault}: rolled {roll}).

fault.burnout: Burnout (10 Damage each use or turn active)

hangar.title: Hangar
hangar.hint: Fighter bays: {fighters}. Spaceship Hangar places: {ships}. Drop a fighter (or a small ship, for a Spaceship Hangar) on this sheet to dock it.
hangar.launchHint: Equipment action: launch one docked craft this round. It appears beside the mothership in the same zone and rolls Initiative.
hangar.oncePerRound: {name} has already launched a craft this round.
hangar.broken: {name}'s hangar is out of action: nothing can launch until it's repaired.
hangar.remote: Flown remotely: it goes dead if the hangar is critically hit, or if the mothership jumps away.
hangar.crewed: Crewed directly: it fights on whatever happens to the mothership.
hangar.fighterDead: {name} loses its remote link and goes dead in space.
hangar.shipHit: {name}, docked in the Spaceship Hangar, takes {damage} Hull damage (Hull {hull}) and is trapped until the hangar is repaired.
hangar.notShip: Only ships can dock in a hangar.
hangar.self: A ship can't dock in itself.
hangar.noFighterHangar: This ship has no Fighter Hangar.
hangar.noShipHangar: This ship has no Spaceship Hangar.
hangar.tooBig: Spaceship Hangars only take small ships.

aegis.impervious: Impervious hull: only AX weapons damage its Hull.
aegis.swarm: Swarm: each hit does 1 Damage plus Burst (flak weapons do full damage).
aegis.axHint: Damages the Hull of Thargoid craft with impervious hulls.
aegis.flakHint: Does full damage against swarms such as Thargons.
aegis.imperviousHint: Only AX weapons damage its Hull; it can't suffer critical hits.
aegis.swarmHint: Hits do 1 Damage plus Burst unless the weapon is flak; it can't suffer critical hits.

honorary.title: Honorary Ranks
honorary.hint: Military Sourcebook. An honorary rank's Social Factor bonus is offered on Social Factor skill rolls with that power.

trade.title: Commodity Market

columnNote.blackMarket: This port has a black market: illegal goods can be bought and sold.

trade.reset: Reset visits to this port (the system has recovered)
trade.hint: The first visit rolls 1d10 + 2; later visits roll 1d10, 1d8, 1d6, then 1d4.
trade.buyOnly: This economy only buys from traders.
trade.footer: Prices are the same to buy or sell. You can't sell a good back in the system where you bought it.

star.primaryHint: Roll on the Primary Star Table, or choose one.
star.inhabitedHint: Most of human space lies in a bubble about 800 light years wide. Uninhabited systems have no civilisation.
star.replaceWarning: Regenerating replaces every star, planet and installation in this system.
star.rewardHint: The total Discovery Reward for every star, planet and moon (Core Rules pp.331–335).
star.gzHint: Water, Earth-like and Ammonia worlds only form at this distance.
star.rerollBody: Reroll this orbit (No Planet removes it)
star.noPlanet: No Planet at {distance}ls: the body is removed.
star.planetEncounter: Planet Encounter (Exploration Supplement): life-bearing or lifeless
star.rerollCiv: Reroll economy, government, allegiance and installations
star.openMarket: Open the Commodity Market for this economy
star.spaceLaneHint: Draw a Space Lane Encounter for this security rating (Super Traders Supplement).
star.noTable: The Roll Tables compendium has no "{name}" table.

mission.title: Mission Generator
mission.countHint: Roll several and combine them into one 'super mission' (same theme).
mission.rankHint: For the suggested rewards per player (p.338). Defaults to the players' most common rank.
mission.makeSystemsHint: Stellar Cartography: create the star systems it asks for (uninhabited) in the Actors sidebar.
mission.rewardLine: Mission Income {mission}, Treasure Income {treasure}. Adjust for how hard the employer thinks it is.
mission.footer: Summaries only: see the page in the Core Rules for the full mission and twist.

turn.title: Turn
turn.starting: Waiting for the turn to start…
turn.speedRange: From Speed {start}: choose {min} to {max} (Accelerate / Decelerate). It stays there for the round.
turn.rechargeDown: Shields down: charging {value} → {after}; they come back at {need} (+{rate}).
turn.obstacleGM: Roll or choose what's in the vehicle's path.
turn.obstacleWaiting: Waiting for the GM to check for obstacles.
turn.noObstaclesHint: Skip the roll: the path is clear this turn.
turn.pilotCheckNeeded: An obstacle: the pilot must make a Vehicle Piloting check.
turn.endEarly: These steps haven't been done: {steps}. End the turn anyway?
turn.watching: Only the GM and this craft's owners can act.
turn.disabled: The turn panel is switched off in the system settings.
turn.cardHint: The turn panel steps through this turn.
turn.noTargets: No other craft on the scene.
turn.pickTargetHint: Pick a target to see what you can do to it.

reason.invalid: {target} can't be targeted by that action now.

between.buttonHint: Earn money between adventures with one of your ships: trading, mining, exploring or bounty hunting (Core Rules p.272).
between.title: Between Adventures: {name}
between.intro: Pick a ship and an activity. You can do this once between adventures, by yourself or by sending an employee.
between.noShips: {name} has no spaceship to work with. Assign a ship to them first.
between.riskHint: Riskier targets pay more. The ship needs enough weapon points (mining lasers don't count).
between.srvHint: Surface exploration with an SRV from the ship's hangar.
between.employeeHint: A crew member does the work instead. They may not come back with the ship.
between.payWages: Crew wages: {wages} for {count} crew, paid first.
between.crewNote: This ship needs a crew of {crew}; {aboard} hired crew signed on for it.

needs.trading: This ship has no cargo rack.
needs.mining: This ship needs a mining laser, a refinery and a cargo rack.
needs.exploration: This ship needs a discovery scanner.
needs.bounty: This ship has only {points} weapon points; Low risk needs more (mining lasers don't count).

sum.trading: Cargo {cargo}t × Trading +{bonus} × the Safe Trading roll per ton.
sum.mining: (Mining {mining} + cargo {cargo}t) × Planetary Knowledge +{bonus} × the mining yield.
sum.bounty: Weapon points {points}. Piloting +{pilot}, Weapons +{guns}. Kill Warrant Scanner +{kws}%.

line.repairs: Both checks failed. D100 {roll}: repairs cost {value}.
line.writtenOff: {ship} is written off instead of repaired.
line.destroyed: Both checks failed by more than 3: {ship} is destroyed.
line.nothing: One check failed: no bounties collected this time.

between.employeeSafe: Employee risk D10 {roll} (lost on {risk}+): they came back with {ship}.
between.employeeLost: Employee risk D10 {roll} (lost on {risk}+): the employee and {ship} never came back.
between.repairsAsk: {ship} needs {cost} of repairs. Pay for them, or write the ship off?
between.shortfall: Short by {amount}: cash can't go below 0.

rare.title: Rare Item Availability
rare.intro: Roll the rare items on sale at this port, by the party's rank (Core Rules p.324).

crew.buttonHint: Hire crew for your ships (Core Rules p.260). They are paid at each Between Adventures.
crew.title: Hire Crew
crew.intro: Roll up crew from the Crew Skill Table.
crew.howHint: In a hurry: take them as rolled. Interviewing takes the place of a Between Adventures roll; you pick from up to six.
crew.wagesNote: Wages are paid at the start of each Between Adventures.
crew.notes: Morality: {morality}. Allegiance: {allegiance}. Salary: {salary} per Between Adventures.

moralityHint.indifferent: Goes along with most things, but may balk at the worst.
moralityHint.principled: Won't act against their allegiance or their conscience.

crew.shipHint: Optional: sign them on for one of your ships. An NPC-flown ship must be fully crewed to earn Between Adventures income.

addiction.title: Addiction: {name}
addiction.choose: {name} is addicted to Combat Stims (cash {cash}). Choose how to deal with it before Between Adventures.
addiction.cured: {name} goes to a clinic ({cost}): cured, but loses 5 Endurance for good and makes no Between Adventures roll.
addiction.habitOk: {name} keeps the habit going ({cost}). D10 {roll}: they survive.
addiction.dies: {name} keeps the habit going. D10 {roll}: their heart gives out. They are dead.
addiction.crippled: {name} can't feed the habit: they are permanently crippled. Only cybernetic surgery can help.
addiction.safe: {name} has used Combat Stims {uses} times this mission. D10 {roll} (addicted on {need} or less): not addicted.
addiction.became: {name} has used Combat Stims {uses} times this mission. D10 {roll} (addicted on {need} or less): addicted!

combined.scaleHint: Combined scale: the target is {scale} scale. Defence +{bonus} for its size; Damage {factor}.
combined.individualHint: Combined scale: assume the target is {range}m away unless the GM says otherwise. Damage {factor}; a natural 10 can cause a critical hit on a ship with its shields down.
combined.attackNote: Against a craft: Damage {factor}, on Shields then Hull.
combined.defenceHint: Includes the bonus for the target's smaller size. Cover is added separately.
combined.coverHintIndividual: Against vehicle and ship weapons: foliage +2, buildings or rocks +4. A shot that misses only because of the cover blows it away.
combined.coverHintVehicle: Against ships, by the obstacle table the vehicle drives on. This cover is never blown away.
combined.noGimbal: Gimballed weapons get no Accuracy bonus against anything but spaceships.
combined.coverBlown: Missed only because of the cover: {name}'s cover is blown away.
combined.noBonuses: Against people: base Damage only, with no Burst or other bonuses.
combined.turretsOnly: {weapon}: a vehicle can only fire turrets (or missiles) at spacecraft.
combined.shipNotClose: {target} isn't in the up-close zone, so it can't be reached from the ground.
combined.vehicleNotClose: {target} isn't in its up-close zone, so it can't be attacked by people.
combined.cantFire: {weapons} can't fire at {target} (only turrets and missiles reach spacecraft).
combined.noTail: No Tailing or Dogfighting across scales.
combined.smallerOnly: Only against smaller units: vehicles or people for a ship.
combined.noRamUp: Only a larger unit can Ram or play Chicken with a smaller one.
combined.shipNoRam: A ship moves too fast to Ram vehicles or people. Use Chicken instead.
combined.noSnipeIndividual: A ship can't Snipe at people.
combined.vehicleVsShip: A vehicle can only attack spacecraft by Snipe or Broadsides.
combined.noFlee: {name} can't Flee while spacecraft are still in the fight.
combined.crawlStop: {name} must be at Speed 0 to Crawl.
combined.turretTargetsHint: Fixed and gimballed weapons all fire at the chosen target. Each turret can fire at any vehicle or ship in its up-close zone, or any person.
combined.runDownRule: A Dodge check against {dn}. You can only run down someone out of cover, or behind cover that wouldn't hurt the vehicle.
combined.chickenVehicleRule: The vehicle rolls D10 + Defence and swerves on {dn} or more.
combined.dodgeRule: A Dodge check against the ship's Defence ({dn}).

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.name: Name
fleet.ownerHint: The character whose craft this is. It appears in their Fleet and is used for their Between Adventures.
fleet.empty: No ships or vehicles. Drag one from the Actors sidebar onto this sheet to add it to the fleet.
fleet.activeHint: Current ship: offered first for Between Adventures.
fleet.releaseConfirm: Take {craft} out of {name}'s fleet? The craft stays in the world.
fleet.noPermission: You don't have permission to change {craft}.
fleet.startIntro: Choose one of the eight starting ships (Core Rules p.38). It is copied from the compendium into your fleet with you as pilot.
fleet.partnerRule: You have a partner: Sidewinders and Eagles are single-seaters, so you need a Hauler or an Adder.
fleet.nameHint: Optional, but recommended: a name of your own tells your ship apart from others of the same model. The model stays on its sheet.
fleet.srvHint: The Sidewinder Discovery comes with a Scarab SRV.
fleet.buildOwnHint: Buy a basic hull and improvements, spending up to {budget}cr. Any money you don't spend is lost. Build it with your GM; this just ticks the step.
fleet.buildOwnChat: {name} is building their own starting ship (up to {budget}cr; unspent credits are lost).

blurb.sidewinderFd4: Fighter-trader: good internal upgrades, accurate weapons and solid defences.
blurb.sidewinderWarden: Attack interceptor for bounty hunters who favour endurance over agility.
blurb.sidewinderDiscovery: Exploration scout, with a Scarab SRV as standard.
blurb.eagleInterceptor: Heavily armed gunfighter that can pull small ships out of supercruise.
blurb.eagleDefender: Short-range dogfighter with balanced weapons and good defences.
blurb.haulerZeta: Roomy trader: big cargo bay, good range, poor defences. Spare cabin for a partner.
blurb.haulerDrigger: Small dedicated miner: earns well between adventures, but a liability in a fight. Spare cabin for a partner.
blurb.adderCornucopia: Mostly unimproved but spacious, with lots of room to upgrade. Two seats: ideal with a partner.

enc.intro: Roll an opponent group by the supplements' Random Generation System: the number of opponents by difficulty, each opponent by the party's Tier.
enc.tierHint: From the party's highest rank. Security groups stop at Tier 3.
enc.humansOnlyHint: For soldiers or unarmed staff: re-roll drones, robots and animals.
enc.title: {difficulty} {faction} group ({scale})
enc.summary: {count} opponents (D10 {roll}), Tier {tier}. {book}, p.{page}. High Threat opponents count as three.

behaviour.thoughtless: thoughtless: closes in and attacks, no cover
behaviour.brute: brute: charges the nearest for melee
behaviour.cunning: cunning: takes cover, keeps 12m off, shoots

enc.placed: Placed {count} hidden tokens on the scene.
enc.noScene: Open a scene first (and roll a group with opponents).
enc.tracking: Tracking reinforcements ({faction}) in this combat: checked at the end of each round.
enc.reinforcementsArrive: Reinforcements: D10 {roll} (+{bonus}) — an Easy group arrives!
enc.alertRaised: Alert check: 10 — the noise raises the Alert!

infil.title: Infiltration
infil.intro: Draw random Infiltration challenges (Espionage Supplement p.45), or tick the ones to choose from. Players split up and take one each; every check in a challenge must pass. A failed challenge can't be retried.
infil.countHint: Ignored if you tick challenges below.
infil.alertOn: Alert: every check one step harder
infil.bribeCost: First pay the mission's Treasure Income.
infil.noActor: Select your token, or set your character in your player configuration.
infil.howTo: Click a skill to roll it for your selected token (or your character). The GM marks each challenge completed or failed.

base.title: Base
base.intro: Create a corporate (Espionage) or military (Military Sourcebook) base to explore room by room.
base.targetHint: With a target, every room rolled adds 5 to the next, and 101+ (or the last room) is the target.
base.alertOn: ALERT: checks one step harder, reinforcements in combat.
base.enterSide: Sneak in by a Side Room
base.doorHint: D10: even, a room; odd, a corridor.
base.corridorDoorHint: Doors in corridors always open into rooms.
base.trackHint: Reinforcements at the end of each round, and (without an Alert) the D10 check for one.
base.rules: Office Workers: 50% ignore you; otherwise ID or an Easy Bluff or Intimidate check. Security groups: Easy Stealth to slip past (Average on Alert). Resisting arrest raises the Alert after two rounds.
base.sideLocked: Locked (D100 {roll}): Easy Security or Average Athletics.
base.doorRoom: The door (D10 {roll}) opens into a room.
base.doorCorridor: The door (D10 {roll}) opens into a corridor.
base.outside: Every room is used: this door leads outside the base.

tools.gmOnly: Only the GM can use this.

planet.surveyHint: Stellar Cartography (5–8): only every fourth lifeless world explored has an encounter.
planet.surveyed: {name} surveyed: no encounter ({n} more lifeless worlds until the next).
planet.treasure: Treasure: the mission's Treasure Income ({amount} each at this rank).
planet.villageArt: They have {item}, but it's a weapon: they only offer artwork worth 100cr. Someone should trade anyway, or offend them.
planet.villageTrade: They offer {item} ({cost}) for one of your weapons.

trap.collapse: D10 {roll}: the wall collapses on {name}: 30 Damage unless an Average Dodge check.
trap.wave: D10 {roll} ({name}): a sickening wave of energy, 10 Damage to the whole team.
trap.beam: D10 {roll}: a yellow beam hits {name}: 40 Damage and their armour destroyed, unless a Hard Dodge check.
trap.clear: D10 {roll} ({name}): no more traps. A chamber of alien technology:

relic.storeroom: D10 {roll}, again: a storeroom of artefacts worth {amount}, and a Rare item. Nothing more to find.

lane.heistNote: Heist: the heist ship (the highest-ranked) launches Hatch Breaker limpets as an Equipment action at cargo-carrying ships with their shields down — Small: {small}; Medium: {medium}; Large: {large} — then collects canisters at the start of its turns. They leave once each pirate has 4 canisters, or after round one if no one carries cargo. Players can submit by dropping half their cargo.

r.offerSafe: D10 {roll}: odd — the old employer lets it go.
r.offerHunted: D10 {roll}: even — the old employer sends bounty hunters.
r.board1: D10 {roll}: abandoned but badly damaged. A Hard Repair check makes it flyable (one try each, players and crew); if all fail it's scrap.
r.board2: D10 {roll}: beyond repair, but its hold is full.
r.board3: D10 {roll}: a trap! Pirates hidden aboard: Easy on a small ship, Medium on a medium one, Hard on a large one. Beat them to salvage it.
r.board4: D10 {roll}: something alive killed the crew. Flee, or fight it:
r.creature: D10 {roll}: {n} × {name}. Beat it to salvage the ship.
r.base1: D10 {roll}: abandoned. Each player and crew member makes a Repair check: that many tons of salvage (Salvage column).
r.base2: D10 {roll}: an illegal trading centre: trade now using column 12 of the Advanced Trading Table.
r.base3: D10 {roll}: an illicit storehouse. Beat a Medium Criminal group; then 3D10 canisters each (Illegal column):
r.base4: D10 {roll}: empty, but with repair facilities: two Field Repairs each (Core p.193).
r.bridge1: D10 {roll}: the confused animal does no harm; have it removed at port.
r.bridge2: D10 {roll}: it cuts the FSD cable. Hunt it down, then Easy Repair to fix the drive.

r.scoop1: D10 {roll}: no problem — the cargo is theirs.
r.scoop2: D10 {roll}: an ambush! A Medium Criminal group.

r.scan3: D10 {roll}: suspicious — detained, and any mission fails. Resisting means a fight.

interdict.title: Interdiction
interdict.intro: Opposed Spaceship Piloting checks (Core p.209): two wins in a row decides it. Pirates and police pick cargo ships first, then multi-role ships, then combat ships.
interdict.bonusHint: Opponents by rank (Super Traders p.45), plus any FSD Interdictor modifier; −5 if the target is larger than its size limit.
interdict.targetHint: The party's current ships, most tempting first.
interdict.howTo: The GM rolls each round, or the target submits.
interdict.pulled: {name} is pulled out of supercruise. Both drop into realspace (10 Hull each; D10 9–10, a component is damaged too).
interdict.escaped: {name} breaks away; {attacker} is forced into realspace.
interdict.component: D10 {roll}: a component is damaged as well.

hostage.payDouble: double pay if it stays this way
hostage.alertOn: Alert: one hostage dies each combat round or skill check.
hostage.negotiatorHint: A player can stay behind to negotiate (Average Bluff or Diplomacy): every later check one step easier.
hostage.negotiatorOn: Negotiating: every check one step easier.
hostage.handHint: Melee and Fighting only, on both sides.
hostage.ambushHint: Burst in: they lose their first turn at Defence 0. Flashbangs only.

outfit.militaryHint: Can be fitted in a military slot (Core Rules p.193).
outfit.strengthHint: Blank: not subject to critical hits.

outfit.fitted: {component} fitted to {ship}{replaced}. Adjust the ship's ratings by hand if it changes them.
outfit.notRoster: {component} isn't subject to critical hits, so it doesn't go on the component roster. Adjust the ship's ratings by hand (Hull, Strength or fuel).
outfit.shipsOnly: Ship components can only be fitted to spaceships.
outfit.tabHint: Drop a Ship Component or Ship Weapon from the compendia on this sheet to fit it (Core Rules pp.192–193). Fixed components must be the hull's class; internal components can't be larger than their slot; military slots take only reinforcement packages and shield cell banks; weapons can't be larger than their hardpoint; and everything together can't draw more power than the power plant makes. The ship's ratings change by what each swap adds or takes away. Old parts sell for 70%.
outfit.payFrom: Pay {cost} from {name}'s credits (and sell what it replaces for 70%)
outfit.sellTo: Sell it to the shipyard for {refund} ({name}'s credits)
outfit.mrpOneGroup: A D-grade Module Reinforcement Package protects one module group: add its Strength to that group's components by hand.

err.bulkheadHull: Those bulkheads are made for the {hull}, not the {ship}.
err.noUtility: This ship has no utility mounts.

silent.hint: Close the heat vents and drop the shields (Core Rules p.268). Hidden from sensors until a scan finds you; then gimballed weapons and automated turrets are at -4 against you, and seekers and torpedoes can't be fired at you. Safe for a minute; then each round the crew take 1D10 Damage and three components 1D10 each. Stopping lets the shields recharge as normal.
silent.sinkHint: Fire a Heat Sink (Equipment Action): another minute of silent running, and +2 Systems against scans this turn (p.198).
silent.scanHint: Actively scan for a silent ship: your Systems + your sensors' General Scan, against its Systems + 4 (small) or + 2 (medium). Win, and your ship can see it.
silent.seenHint: Ships whose scans have found this one: they can target it.
silent.started: {name} goes silent running: shields down, hidden from sensors. Safe for {rounds} rounds.
silent.stopped: {name} stops silent running. Its shields recharge as normal from next turn.
silent.sinkUsed: {name} fires a Heat Sink: another minute of silent running, and +2 Systems against scans this turn ({left}/{max} left).
silent.sinkWasted: {name} fires a Heat Sink ({left}/{max} left). It isn't silent running, so it only cools the ship.
silent.sinkActive: {name} has already fired a Heat Sink this turn.
silent.noShields: {name} is silent running: its shields are off.
silent.noRecharge: Silent running: the shields stay off.
silent.roundNote: {name} is silent running ({left} safe rounds left).
silent.overheating: {name} has been silent running too long and overheats!
silent.componentOut: {name} takes {n} Damage and is knocked out ({after}/{max}).
silent.hidden: {target} is silent running and hidden from your sensors: scan for it first.
silent.noGuided: {weapon} can't lock on to {target}: it's silent running.
silent.attackNote: Silent running: +4 Defence against gimballed weapons and automated turrets.
silent.noneHidden: No ship here is hidden from you.
